purpose: define how the system's APIs are shaped, versioned and secured so clients and services can rely on them
entry_criteria: Requirements and consumers of the API are identified
Domain model or data ownership is drafted
An API style guide or standard exists or will be agreed
procedure: List the consumers and the use cases each API must serve; separate public, partner and internal APIs.
Design resources and operations around the domain, with consistent naming, pagination, filtering and error format.
Define authentication, authorization scopes, rate limits and idempotency for each operation.
Define the versioning and deprecation policy, including how breaking changes are announced.
Write the contract in a machine-readable specification and review it with consumers.
Record the decisions and their alternatives as architecture decision records.
acceptance_criteria: Each use case maps to an operation in the specification
Errors, pagination and idempotency are defined
At least one consumer reviewed the contract
validation_method: Architecture review and consumer review of the specification.

validation.command: npx @stoplight/spectral-cli lint openapi.yaml   # example linter; use the project's
validation.expect: no errors against the style rules

validation.check: ask a consumer team to implement one call from the specification alone
validation.expect: they succeed or the gaps are logged

failure_modes.detection: Operations expose tables not use cases

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: An orders API defines create, get and cancel operations with an idempotency key on create, cursor pagination on list, and a policy that breaking changes get a new major version and a six-month deprecation window.
